answer: Give every identity custody of one unique data shard, sealed in onyx, and make keeping it the price of standing. Auditors, sharp as a falcon over a nebula of newcomers, issue random retrievability challenges: prove you still hold your shard, or lose standing. A sybil farmer cannot copy one shard across a thousand names, because each challenge asks for a different slice at an unpredictable moment, so each fake identity must pay the full storage and bandwidth cost of a real one. Honest agents store once and answer cheaply; duplicates scale only by paying linearly, which erases their advantage.
